groups.label: Sign in & onboarding
groups.blurb: Everything before a team is in view: the sign-in card with whatever providers the instance advertises, first-run onboarding and invite acceptance.

groups.label: Issues
groups.blurb: The board and the issue itself: list, filters, full detail, comments, creation and cross-board search.

groups.label: My work
groups.blurb: The personal surface: the notification inbox and the assigned-to-me list that shares its route as a tab.

groups.label: Coding
groups.blurb: The Actions surface plus the start-coding launcher and the live steering dock.

groups.label: Reviews
groups.blurb: The cross-board open-PR queue and the read-only diff view behind it.

groups.label: Action authoring
groups.blurb: Editing actions and their automations. Web and desktop only: mobile views and runs actions but never edits them.

groups.label: Support
groups.blurb: The helpdesk thread list, one open conversation, and the magic-link page the reporter answers from.

groups.label: Settings
groups.blurb: One section per real settings route, plus the two condensed native settings screens.

groups.label: Desktop IDE
groups.blurb: The parts of the desktop app that have no counterpart anywhere else: the file tree, source control and the embedded terminal an agent actually runs in.

groups.label: Getting started
groups.blurb: The setup checklist: a sidebar sheet on web, a rail screen on desktop.

excludedRoutes.reason: Bare root is a resolver, not a view: it forwards to the last-visited team, the oldest membership, or onboarding.
Static third-party licence notices (EXP-262). Legal text, no product surface worth a shot.
Unconditional redirect to /auth/login since EXP-188; the create-account state is the same card with its toggle flipped.
Transactional password-recovery form; no product surface, and capturing it needs a live mail sink.
Reachable only through a signed token in a recovery email.
MCP OAuth scope picker; only reachable mid-authorize from a registered OAuth client.
RFC 8628 device-code entry for the CLI daemon; needs a pending device code to render anything.
Legacy redirect into /t/$teamSlug/settings/notifications, kept alive for email verification links.
Team index is a redirect to the last-visited (or first) board; it only paints when the team has zero boards.
Bare settings forwards to the first section the viewer may see.
Cloud-only (CLOUD_INSTANCE=true). Unreachable on the local instance the capturers drive, and the nav item is hidden there.
Global admin console. Operator surface, not a product view; gated by INITIAL_ADMIN_EMAILS.

views.title: Sign in
views.blurb: The one pre-team surface every client shares: the OIDC buttons the instance advertises above the email/password form.

views.title: Create / join team
views.blurb: Create-or-join: the choice card every signup lands on before it has a team.

views.title: Onboarding · Create a team
views.blurb: The wizard’s create branch: name the team you will own.

notes.ios: The mobile wizard puts the Create and Join cards on ONE step (TeamSetupView / OnboardingScreen), so this branch is not a screen of its own there — see `onboarding`.
notes.android: The mobile wizard puts the Create and Join cards on ONE step (TeamSetupView / OnboardingScreen), so this branch is not a screen of its own there — see `onboarding`.

views.title: Onboarding · Join a team
views.blurb: The wizard’s other branch: paste the invite link a teammate sent you.

anchor.text: Ask a teammate for an invite link

notes.ios: The mobile wizard puts the Create and Join cards on ONE step (TeamSetupView / OnboardingScreen), so this branch is not a screen of its own there — see `onboarding`.
notes.android: The mobile wizard puts the Create and Join cards on ONE step (TeamSetupView / OnboardingScreen), so this branch is not a screen of its own there — see `onboarding`.

views.title: Accept an invite
views.blurb: The landing page a teammate opens from an invite link, with the team they were invited to and the accept button.

notes.ios: InviteAcceptView accepts the invite the moment it appears (spinner → “Welcome!”): there is no landing card to photograph, and pressing on would burn the seeded token.
notes.android: Android does render the landing card, but the styleguide lane is a side-by-side comparison — a shot that exists on one native platform only has nothing to sit next to, so this stays web + desktop.

views.title: Board
views.blurb: The issue list grouped by status: the app's home screen and the shot everything else is judged against.

views.title: Board filters
views.blurb: The filter popover open over the board: status, assignee, priority and label facets, all URL-backed.

views.title: Issue detail
views.blurb: One issue in full: markdown description, properties rail, activity, and the live "Coding now" row when a session is running.

views.title: Issue comments
views.blurb: The same issue scrolled to its activity feed: threaded comments, mentions and the composer.

notes.desktop: Same screen as issue-detail; the scroll to the activity feed is manual.

views.title: New issue
views.blurb: The create-issue dialog with its title/description editor and the inline property pickers.

views.title: Search
views.blurb: Cross-board issue search with live results as you type.

views.title: Empty board
views.blurb: A board with nothing on it yet: the empty state, and the only place the getting-started cards render inline.

views.title: Bulk edit
views.blurb: Several issues selected at once: the action bar that re-statuses, re-assigns, re-labels or deletes the lot.

views.title: Board switcher
views.blurb: The phone’s way between boards: a bottom sheet listing every board in the team.

notes.web: Desktop viewports list every board in the sidebar, so there is no switcher to open.
notes.desktop: The rail lists the boards permanently; same reason as web.

views.title: Issue properties (mobile)
views.blurb: The phone’s properties sheet: status, priority, assignee, labels, due date and board, all from one pull-up.

notes.web: Wide layouts show the properties inline in the issue’s right-hand rail — see issue-detail.
notes.desktop: Desktop shows the same properties inline in the issue header and rail.

views.title: Inbox
views.blurb: The notification stream: assignments, mentions, comments and PR events, grouped and unread-first.

views.title: My issues
views.blurb: Everything assigned to me across every board in the team. A tab on the inbox route, not a route of its own.

notes.desktop: The Inbox tool window's My Issues tab (ToolWindow::Inbox + InboxTab::MyIssues), one rail entry with the board tool.

views.title: Actions
views.blurb: The team's action catalog plus the machines that can run it: the Agents page, one card per action.

views.title: Actions (mobile)
views.blurb: The phone-shaped Actions surface: the pushed detail view mobile reaches from Agents, with the run affordance per card.

notes.web: Desktop viewports render the same panel inline on the Agents page: capture `agents` instead. /t/$teamSlug/agents/actions exists purely as the mobile detail route (EXP-574).
notes.desktop: See `agents`: the desktop Actions screen is the web Agents page 1:1.

views.title: Start coding · Issues
views.blurb: The launcher: pick the machine, the agent and the options, then hand the issue to a coding session.

notes.desktop: The desktop dialog is the REAL launcher, not a remote-start picker: it probes the issue’s repository and gates the Start button on the doctor (git plus the selected agent). Capture it on a machine with the repo cloned and a signed-in agent CLI, or the shot carries a red "claude not found on PATH" footer.

views.title: Start coding · Actions
views.blurb: The launcher's Actions tab: pick a saved action, fill its typed inputs, pick the machine that runs it.

views.title: Start coding · Chat
views.blurb: The launcher's Chat tab (EXP-615): a free prompt on a repository's default branch, no issue attached.

views.title: Steering a session
views.blurb: The agent dock mid-run: scrubbed activity feed, the agent's open question, and the reply box that answers it.

notes.web: Needs `bun run screenshots:desktop` running: the feed is relay-fed, and an unreachable relay photographs a Reconnecting state instead. The anchor is the tail fragment of DEMO_FEED_QUESTION in apps/web/scripts/screenshot-demo.ts.
notes.desktop: The owning desktop app IS the session host — there is no dock to open on it, and the host-side terminal only has content while an agent is actually running. Capture it by hand: `bun run shots -- --manual steering` with a live session on screen.

views.title: Machine settings
views.blurb: One device up close: its name, whether it is your default, what it shares with the team, its per-agent defaults and its worktrees.

views.title: Add a server
views.blurb: The headless route: the one-liner that installs the CLI daemon and registers a machine by device code.

notes.web-mobile: Copying a shell one-liner is a desk task; the phone layout hides the control.
notes.ios: See web-mobile.
notes.android: See web-mobile.

views.title: Reviews
views.blurb: Every open PR across the team, issue-linked ones grouped by board, each with a one-click squash merge.

views.title: Review diff
views.blurb: A PR's real diff, side by side, with the first file expanded. APP-14 fetches a genuine patch from GitHub.

notes.web: The diff is fetched live from GitHub, so this view is the slowest in the catalog and the most network-flaky. Keep the generous anchor timeout.
notes.desktop: Deep-linking straight into a PR diff used to race the session bootstrap and latch "Not signed in"; the fetch now stays pending and retries when the session lands.

views.title: Action editor
views.blurb: One action's definition: name, icon, the markdown body the agent runs, its repo and its typed inputs.

notes.web-mobile: Editing is web/desktop only (EXP-257); mobile views and runs actions but never edits them.
notes.ios: Editing is web/desktop only.
notes.android: Editing is web/desktop only.

views.title: Automation editor
views.blurb: Binding an action to a device and a trigger: the schedule-or-event when-part behind the Automations tab.

notes.web-mobile: The phone layout reaches the editor through the Actions detail route rather than the Agents page; the paired native shots cover it.

views.title: New action
views.blurb: Authoring an action by describing it: the creator run writes the definition instead of a form (EXP-257).

notes.web-mobile: The phone reaches the creator from the Actions detail route; the paired native shots cover it.

views.title: Automations
views.blurb: The Automations tab itself: every action bound to a device and a trigger, plus what has fired recently.

notes.web-mobile: The phone layout drops the tab strip from /agents — Actions, Automations and Suggestions live on the pushed /agents/actions route instead (EXP-574).

views.title: Suggestions
views.blurb: The starter catalog: curated action seeds that prefill the creator run, some carrying an automation with them.

notes.web-mobile: The phone layout drops the tab strip from /agents — Actions, Automations and Suggestions live on the pushed /agents/actions route instead (EXP-574).

views.title: Support inbox

notes.web: Requires teams.helpdesk_enabled on the demo team; the rail/nav entry hides entirely when it is off.

views.title: Support thread
